gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-gowun-batang: Gowun Batang has a literary softness, its terminals cut back to leave big gaps, under Bruno Ace's constant-width display lines. Gowun Batang carries paragraph after paragraph with a refined, unhurried pace, never fighting the heading above it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-habibi: Distinctive and expressive, Bruno Ace draws every letter in one continuous line. Habibi, with a clear channel leading into each round letter, gives extended reading a traditional, editorial rhythm.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-kay-pho-du: A ruler-drawn, constant-width line defines Bruno Ace, with counters that stay connected to the outside. But Kay Pho Du, with counters like a hollow reed cut open, brings a classic, traditional counterweight beneath it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-labrada: Bruno Ace holds one uninterrupted line width across every letter. Labrada, a serif with wide openings on small letters, gives that display heading a dignified, bookish counterpart waiting below.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-laila: Laila reads traditional and editorial, with generous space between curve ends and stems. Bruno Ace's letters look like thin steel rod bent into shape, and that display character against Laila's open serif is the whole appeal.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-montaga: Straight lines, soft stitches: Montaga's pen-lifted curves leave loops unfinished, like thread run along a path. Bruno Ace handles the expressive display work, while Montaga takes the bookish, editorial reading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-new-tegomin: Dignified in tone, New Tegomin makes its c a wide-open ring, sitting beneath Bruno Ace's marker-like, constant line. Over a full page, the reading feels traditional and steadily composed.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-podkova: Podkova is bookish and traditional, its c broad and welcoming. Paragraph after paragraph stays inviting in Podkova, while Bruno Ace's strokes, like toothpaste squeezed in one steady line, hold the heading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-rhodium-libre: Brush ends lift away; the ruled lines stay put. The tension between Bruno Ace's one-width t and Rhodium Libre's lifted brush ends is what makes this pairing worth a look.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-rokkitt: Bruno Ace has tubular strokes, like bent copper pipe. Next to it, Rokkitt feels bookish and traditional, its c as open as a bent paperclip, so the two read like pieces of one workshop.
